## Fast-slow system {auto-animate=true .center}
  \begin{cases} 
    \dot X^\epsilon_t = f(X^\epsilon_t, Y^\epsilon_t)  \\  
    Y^\epsilon_t \text{ oscillates fast }
  \end{cases}


## Averaging Principle {auto-animate=true .center}
::: {.callout-note}
## Under appropriate regularity conditions 
Suppose 
$$
\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T b(x, Y^\epsilon_s) \, ds = \bar b(x) \,.
$$
Then $X^\epsilon \to  X$, where
$$
\dot X_t = \bar b(X_t) \,.
$$
:::

_Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems_, @FreidlinWentzellRandomPerturbations2012


## Random fast system {.center}

\begin{cases} 
  d X^\epsilon_t &= f(X^\epsilon, Y^\epsilon_t, t) dt + G(X^\epsilon, Y^\epsilon_t, t) dW^1_t \\  
  \epsilon d Y^\epsilon_t  &=  g(X^\epsilon_t,  Y^\epsilon_t)dt + \sqrt{\epsilon} \sigma(X^\epsilon_t, Y^\epsilon_t) dW^2_t
\end{cases}




## Rate of convergence {.center}
::: {.callout-note}
## Under appropriate regularity conditions

Given $T>0$ and $\varphi \in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$. There exists a constant $C$ such that
\begin{equation}
        \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \mathbb E \left| X^\epsilon_t - Z^\epsilon_t  \right| \leq C\epsilon^{1/2}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
        \sup_{t\in [0, T]} \left| \mathbb E \varphi(X^\epsilon_t) - \mathbb E \varphi(Z^\epsilon_t)  \right|
        \leq C \epsilon \,.
\end{equation}
:::
@RocknerSunXieStrongWeak2019
